clue.text: Decide length, cutting piece of cake

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing sits inside it, so the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy, like a piece of cake
L is the standard abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Someone choosing how long a slice to cut from a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside CINCH after its first letter, giving CLINCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal or argument is to settle it conclusively, which is to decide it.

clue.text: Limit a large town's power

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit
taken as written
a city is a large town; the 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: Restricting the authority of a big municipality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the apostrophe s as 'is': limit + a + large town is power.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity can mean the ability or power to do something, as in a capacity for hard work.

clue.text: Demon with strength having no time for deadlock

parts.note: an imp is a small demon

indicators.note: no time means the letter abbreviating time is removed from the word for strength

parts.note: an asset is a strength, a useful quality
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A devil with great power but no time to spare for a stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength' first suggests power or might; think of a strength as a good point in your favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, the same idea as a stalemate or deadlock.

clue.text: Belief about party led by Conservative

indicators.note: led by says the following piece goes in front of the others

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
re means about or concerning
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A political conviction concerning a party headed by a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a political party, but it is the social kind, a do.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a set of beliefs or principles, from the Latin for I believe, so it is a statement of belief.

clue.text: Dash about, beset by mass hatred

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so the short word sits within the longer

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
odium is widespread hatred or disgust
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A runner charging around, surrounded by a hostile crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: M and ODIUM form the outer shell, and C sits inside ODIUM between I and U.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of something is a small amount, as in a dash of milk; a modicum is likewise a small quantity.

clue.text: Citrus fruit supplied by chap, bold European, around North African port

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: around says the word for bold encloses the port's name

parts.note: daring means bold or adventurous
Oran is a port city in Algeria
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Fruit shipped in from a North African harbour by an adventurous European trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Oran is Algeria's second city, a Mediterranean port; it sits inside the word for bold, not next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandarin orange is a small, loose-skinned variety of citrus, close kin to the tangerine.

clue.text: Remove unnecessary items left, say, after December

indicators.note: after places the pieces behind the month abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation
L is the abbreviation for left
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A January clear-out after the Christmas clutter of December.
explanation.definitionFit: To declutter a room is to clear away the clutter, getting rid of things not needed.

clue.text: Sign of sharp bend in road in Switzerland, twisting over mountain finally

definitions.text: Sign of sharp bend in road

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

indicators.note: twisting suggests bending out of shape, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

indicators.note: finally keeps only the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A warning sign on a winding Swiss Alpine road.
explanation.walkthrough: CH comes from the Latin Confoederatio Helvetica on Swiss car plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrons are the V-shaped black-and-white arrows placed on roadsides to warn drivers of a sharp curve.

clue.text: Animal in line following mother

indicators.note: following puts the line abbreviation behind the word for mother

parts.note: mamma is a familiar word for mother
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A young creature walking in single file behind its mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In line' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is only a link and 'line' alone gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal is a warm-blooded vertebrate that feeds its young on milk, one class of animal.

clue.text: Demo kept moving, not quietly in parts, creating alarms

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for parts

parts.note: sectors are parts or divisions of something

indicators.note: moving letters change position, so these two words are rearranged
quietly is p, the musical piano marking, and not says it is dropped

parts.note: taken letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: A protest march that kept going noisily through several districts, causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the P from DEMO KEPT, rearrange the rest, and put it after the first S of SECTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke detectors are devices that sound a warning when they sense smoke, so they are alarms.

clue.text: Sweet temper a prince abandoned, interrupting head of government

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into its middle, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: the Prime Minister heads the British government

indicators.note: abandoned behaviour is unrestrained and wild, so those letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: three words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A royal heir loses his temper and barges in on a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen jumbled letters sit between the P and M of PM, giving PEPPERMINT CREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint cream is a mint-flavoured confection, so it is a type of sweet, the British word for a candy.

clue.text: Clerical garment found with odd items of classy clobber

indicators.note: odd items are those in the first, third and fifth positions of the word that follows

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word
to clobber someone is to hit them, and so is to sock them

explanation.surface: A smart item of dress turning up among stylish clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothing, which suits the surface, but here it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is the long, close-fitting robe worn by priests and choristers, so it is a churchman's garment.

clue.text: Article as broadcast about tanks

parts.note: the indefinite article
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, i.e. as

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word before it runs backwards

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An editorial piece about military tanks, as heard on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Qua is Latin used in English for 'in the role of'; 'tanks' points to the military, but these hold fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass containers for keeping fish, so they are fish tanks rather than armoured vehicles.

clue.text: Step inside theatre, admitted

indicators.note: inside tells us the letters lie within the run of words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: An invitation to come into a playhouse now that you have been let in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is the flat horizontal part of a stair you put your foot on, which is a step.

clue.text: Flirtation beginning to damage partnership

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
an alliance is a partnership or union

explanation.surface: A casual romance starts to wreck a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or sexual involvement, light and not serious, much like a flirtation.

clue.text: Living without purpose? Find grit to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two words taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice to an aimless person: develop some determination and change your ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone drifting moves through life aimlessly, without direction or goals, hence the question mark for the descriptive phrase.

clue.text: Firm route including road, large and yellow

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the route word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a way is a route
Rd is the abbreviation for road
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A company's route takes in a big yellow road, like a road atlas legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a road-map colour, but it means lacking courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is informal for cowardly, lacking the courage to face danger.

clue.text: Fight, protecting rear, without a dagger

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it on all sides, so the fight word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter a is taken out of the word for rear

parts.note: the tail is the rear end of an animal or vehicle

explanation.surface: A brawl in which someone shields their backside while unarmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a dagger' reads as unarmed, but 'without a' is the instruction and 'dagger' alone is the definition. A set-to is British for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short knife with a narrow tapering blade, a kind of dagger.

clue.text: Modified material for jacket perhaps worn by a king

indicators.note: something worn by a person is around them, so the cloth word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: tweed is a rough woollen cloth often made into jackets
taken as written
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A tailored jacket altered for a monarch to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: A and K go inside TWEED between E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak something is to make a small adjustment, so tweaked means slightly modified.

clue.text: See me in love repeatedly faced by resistance

definitions.text: See me in love repeatedly faced by resistance

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the doubled letter that follows it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O, here written twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover keeps falling for someone despite opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Shakespeare's Romeo falls for Rosaline then Juliet, and his love meets resistance from the feuding families.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is Shakespeare's young lover, forever falling for someone and opposed by both households, so the clue describes him.

clue.text: Supervise fool in dock

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on an idiot who is on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a courtroom, but it is the verb for tying up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to observe and check it over time, which is to supervise it.

clue.text: Rouse scattered tribes

indicators.note: scattered means strewn about, so the next word's letters lose their order

parts.note: taken letter for letter as material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Gathering together dispersed peoples to take action.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestir yourself is to get moving and make an effort, so it means to rouse or stir into activity.

clue.text: Soldier in middle of foreign field, cold and mournful

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the word that comes next

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the letters that follow it

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field
GI is an American soldier
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A soldier lying in a foreign field evokes Rupert Brooke's poem 'The Soldier', cold and sad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Brooke's First World War line about 'some corner of a foreign field'; lea is a poet's word for a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means in the manner of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so it means sorrowful and mournful.

clue.text: Lawyer after anger discounting thousand extra items

indicators.note: after tells us the lawyer comes behind the other piece in the answer
discounting means leaving out of the reckoning, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to madden someone is to anger them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
a DA is an American District Attorney

explanation.surface: A legal bill tacking on charges after a fee dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, District Attorney, is an American public prosecutor; 'thousand' is the Roman numeral that the anger word sheds.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda is the plural of addendum, things added at the end of a book or document, so they are extra items.

clue.text: Like match won by neither side, tense

definitions.text: Like match won by neither side
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a game ending level
second meaning: looking strained and haggard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' might suggest grammar, but here it describes a strained, haggard face.
explanation.definitionFit: A match ending level is called this, and a face pinched with worry or tiredness is described the same way.

clue.text: Impressed, raved about fake, endlessly accepted without question

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to be taken with something is to be impressed by it
to forge something is to fake it
to rant about something is to rave about it

explanation.surface: An art critic who was taken in, then ranted about the forgery he had swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: FORGE loses its final E; the pieces go TAKEN, FORG, RANTED, giving TAKEN FOR GRANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken for granted is assumed true or available without being questioned or valued.

clue.text: Communists keeping resolution? Correct

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the communists word surrounds the other

parts.note: Reds is a common nickname for communists
res is a standard abbreviation for resolution, as of a screen or a motion

explanation.surface: Party members asking whether they are right to stick to a resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong or imbalance is to set it right, so redress as a verb means to correct.

clue.text: Vitality needed by keener gymnasts

indicators.note: needed by suggests the letters are contained within the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Athletes who are especially eager require plenty of pep.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitality is liveliness and vigour, which is what having lots of energy means.
